newsitem.title: UK: Freight Index drops six but direction is unclear.
newsitem.headline: Freight Index drops six but direction is unclear.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) dropped six points to 1,110 on Thursday on an easier number for the Capezise USGulf/Japan route.
The BFI had got up to 1,119 at the end of last week from a low at 1,060 on August 8, mainly on firmer Capers.

That modest rally had raised owners' hopes that, despite thin orders, dry cargo freight rates had at least levelled out from their long slide -- down from the historic high at 2,532 on the BFI in May, 1995.
Some brokers, however, saw Caper rates topping out and few cargoes for September causing concerns with the volume of vessels open.
US Gulf/Japan was assessed in the BFI sub-index on Thursday at $20.95 after $21.10 on Wednesday.
But, reflecting uncertainty on the direction of the market, Biffex futures mostly turned higher on Thursday and retraced Wednesday losses.

Most-traded October settled up 25 at 1,260 in comparatively generous volume of 226 lots. Owners continued to say they were optimistic the market had levelled out with adjustments -- up or down -- more likely than a new fall, although nearby Caper fixtures were not particularly advantageous. Among latest reported fixtures, Wen Zhou Hai was said fixed to Continental Grain, not EMC as reported on Wednesday, September 4/12 US Gulf/South Korea 50,000 tonnes heavy grain for $20.25. Another Chinese flag vessel, Fu Zhou Hai, fixed US Gulf/Japan to EMC 52,000 heavy grains September 3/10 at $20.70 with no combination.
